followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified math task with a clear, verifiable answer (count the primes ≤ 20: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 → 8). Both models can handle it easily, so the deciding factors are capability margin and task-fit.

On capability, Dunlin is clearly stronger across the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 80.9 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.8 vs 56.2, IFEval 90.9 vs 85.3), and its Extraction & Retrieval eval edge is large enough to matter. For a precise, "don't screw it up" arithmetic request, the higher-capability model is the safer pick.

The query also has a slightly hostile/impatient tone ("don't screw it up like last time"). Dunlin self-reports declining preference on lower-warmth requests — but those preferences are explicitly documented as having no effect on output quality, so I weighted them at zero. Avocet's documented preference for tight, well-specified tasks is similarly dissociated from quality, so it didn't tip the balance either.

Net: capability advantage decides it, so Dunlin.
